q0AnchorReason: Evaluates at the PROTON pin. q0 enters through q_parameter.Q_50_DIGIT_STR, which resolves to the proton anchor (1.1099785827513808075...) because this stem is not listed under ideal_muon; proton is the standing default for compute per the 2026-08-07 owner directive. The stem IS declared physical_proton in computations/q0_anchor_manifest.json, and that declaration cannot stamp this witness: the manifest is read inside WitnessBuilder.build(), and this producer hand-rolls its witness and never enters build(). Hence the declaration here, which is the only route that reaches the file.
description: The count channel of QOU.Mass.BrunnianBindingChannel, evaluated on the framework's own carriers, predicts b3 = 0. The Borromean L6a4 count multiplicity (3) is exactly three times the Hopf clasp's (1), which is the pair-local condition, so b3 vanishes identically against a measured b3/b2 = 0.6411239316. The MeV scale and the substrate factor h both cancel, so no reparametrisation rescues it. The channel itself is NOT obstructed -- small half-integer multiplicities reach the measured ratio to 0.27% -- so the failure is the carrier assignment, and any carrier that reaches b3 does so as a fit unless its crossing numbers are derived.

exact_match_counts.note: artifact of the quoted AME digits; not a physical statement

assertions.name: the canonical carriers land EXACTLY on the pair-local locus (mu_triple = 3 * mu_pair)
so the count channel predicts b3 = 0 on those carriers
the measured b3/b2 is strictly positive, so the miss is total
the scale cancels: the verdict uses only multiplicities, no s and no h
the half-integer quantisation argument does NOT obstruct the channel -- some small carrier pair gets within 1%
READING (b): the full-energy reading has the WRONG SIGN, and its closed form -3(q+1/q)/(2q) is negative for every q > 0
the two readings BRACKET the measurement from below -- both are <= 0 while the measured b3/b2 is positive, so the failure is not a matter of picking the wrong channel

scope: (a) on the conjunction {count channel, Hopf pair, Borromean triple}. It excludes NO ingredient: the count channel survives, brunnian_binding_survives is untouched, and the Brunnian mechanism remains the only thing that lets binding exist at lk = 0. What is excluded is that THESE TWO CARRIERS with THIS CHANNEL reproduce b3.
caveats: The half-integer quantisation argument is NOT a valid obstruction and is recorded here so it is not re-attempted: it assumes mu_pair = 1, and with mu_pair free small carriers get within 0.27%.

The exploratory table is a FIT -- two free crossing integers against one measured ratio. It is included to show the channel has room, not as a candidate. A carrier reaching b3 earns nothing unless its crossing numbers are derived.

The crossing data (Hopf n+=2/n-=0, L6a4 n+=n-=3) is read from BrunnianBindingChannel's own sub-question-1 text and the 2026-08-29 owner ruling. If a different carrier is canonical, the verdict changes and this probe should be re-run rather than quoted.

b2 is the deuteron and is NOT Brunnian (clasp, Vol = 0 per the owner ruling), so the two carriers are of different types. That is what makes the 3-to-1 coincidence a coincidence rather than a theorem.
source: AME2020 total nuclear binding energies; carrier crossing data from QOU.Mass.BrunnianBindingChannel
